filename: Modern air-sea flux distributions reduce uncertainty in the future ocean carbon sink.pdf
title: Modern air-sea flux distributions reduce uncertainty in the future ocean carbon sink
testbed_rationale: This study analyzes existing CMIP6 and MAGICC7 projections alongside eight existing observation-based pCO2 flux products, performing simple offset adjustments rather than creating an ML training/evaluation benchmark.
pain_points: Large quantitative spread across ESMs in 21st-century ocean carbon sink projections (up to 50 PgC in CMIP6 and 120 PgC in MAGICC7).
Sparsity of direct ocean observations introduces uncertainty in modern observation-based flux estimates.
Significant regional and zonal-mean discrepancies between ESM air-sea CO2 fluxes and observation-derived products (e.g., Southern Ocean sink vs source).
extraction_notes: The paper uses products generated by ML methods (e.g., neural networks, SOMs), but does not itself train or develop machine learning models.
